description: Machine appended boilerplate, per the DISCLAIMER convention in docs/annotation-guide.md: text attached by a system, gateway or template independently of what the sender wrote. Matching is on the block as a whole. Deliberately generic: patterns target the shapes that recur across senders, not any one vendor's template, because fitting a single sender's footer would not transfer.

phrases.pattern: (if you (have received|are not) .{0,80}(in error|the intended recipient)|please (notify the sender|delete) .{0,60}(immediately|and delete))
(accepts? no (liability|responsibility)|any views or opinions (presented|expressed) .{0,60}are (solely )?those of the (author|sender))
(vertrauliche Informationen|Diese E-?Mail (ist|enthält) .{0,60}vertraulich|Sollten Sie nicht der richtige Adressat sein)

phrases.comment: The bare word destinatario used to be an alternative on its own, so any Spanish sentence mentioning a recipient counted as a 0.9 disclaimer. The recipient reference now needs its boilerplate context.
phrases.pattern: (Este (mensaje|correo) .{0,60}confidencial|informaci.n confidencial|uso exclusivo de(l)? destinatario|si (usted )?no es el destinatario)

phrases.comment: The bare token GDPR and the bare phrase privacy policy both appear in ordinary work prose, so each alternative now needs its footer context.
phrases.pattern: ((see|view|read|review|check) (our|the) privacy (notice|policy)|privacy (notice|policy)\s*[:|]|in accordance with (the )?(GDPR|General Data Protection Regulation)|process(es|ing)? (of )?your personal data|isikuandmete töötlemise)

phrases.comment: The bare word unsubscribe also appears in prose about mailing lists, so it only counts standing alone on its own line, which is the bare-link-text shape, or with its imperative footer context.
phrases.pattern: (to unsubscribe|unsubscribe (from|at|here|now|at any time)|click here to unsubscribe|^\s*unsubscribe\s*\.?\s*$|if you (no longer |don'?t )?(wish|want) to (receive|get)|opt out of these emails|manage your (email )?preferences|loobu (uudiskirjast|teavitustest))

phrases.comment: Italian, Portuguese, Dutch, Polish, Russian, Finnish and Scandinavian mail all had reply-header coverage but no disclaimer coverage at all. These are the standard legalese openings, same shape as the English and German entries.
phrases.pattern: (Le informazioni contenute .{0,60}(riservat|confidenzial)|Questo messaggio .{0,60}(riservat|confidenzial)|Se non siete il destinatario)
(this is an? (automated|automatic|system.generated) (e-?mail|message|notification)|please do not reply to this (e-?mail|message)|do not reply directly to this)

phrases.comment: The canonical notification footer: why you got this and how to stop it. Recurs across almost every service.
Opt out and preference management, distinct from a plain unsubscribe link.
Standing promotional footer on a notification: an invitation to subscribe to something other than what the message is about.
phrases.pattern: (want to (know|hear|stay|learn) .{0,80}\?\s*(would you|subscribe|sign up|join)|would you like to (stay|be) (up.to.date|informed|notified) .{0,60}\?)

phrases.comment: Provider branding appended by the sending platform. Case sensitive on purpose: under the i flag the capital brand class matched any word, so prose like 'I sent via courier yesterday' counted as branding. The line anchor keeps it to the standalone footer shape.
Standing support or help pointer in a service footer.
